I actually skipped a bit and started reading from what happens when SCP-7789-J is activated (without reading what causes it), and my god it was actually pretty disturbing, made me think why a seemingly real skip was in the jokes section.

Then I burst out laughing when I went back up to read what caused all this.

So what I'm saying is, maybe we could change this article to make the phone more of a punchline than it is at the moment? Mention what causes activation later in the article.

item.content:encoded: I have been noticing an increasing number of used of the word "on" when "in" or "to" would be more appropriate. I am not sure if this is because the individuals who wrote those things are non-native, or if it's an emerging shift in language with the younger folk.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I had not a single reaction to this article while reading it. Well, other than noting that "on airplane mode" in this context doesn't quite work; "in" should be the preposition in all cases other than "forcibly set (to)". I mean, that reads better to me at least.
